name: How long does a walk-in shower installation take in an occupied Los Angeles home?

mainEntity.name: How long does a walk-in shower installation usually take if the bathroom is being remodeled while people are still living in the house?
mainEntity.text: How long does a walk-in shower installation usually take if the bathroom is being remodeled while people are still living in the house?

acceptedAnswer.text: A standard walk-in shower installation usually takes about 1 to 3 weeks, but occupied homes in Los Angeles often need a more careful schedule. Living in the house can slow the project because crews may work around family routines, protect nearby rooms, and limit noisy or messy tasks to certain hours. The biggest timeline variables are demolition, plumbing changes, waterproofing, tile complexity, custom glass lead times, and unexpected subfloor or wall repairs. If the bathroom is the only one in the home, the project may need phased work or temporary bathing arrangements. The best way to avoid delays is to finalize the layout, fixtures, tile, and glass details before work starts and ask for a clear sequence of milestones. A good contractor should explain when the shower will be unusable, when water can be turned back on, and what daily access the household will have during construction.
acceptedAnswer.description: Most walk-in shower installations take 1 to 3 weeks, but occupied homes often need extra time for dust protection, daily cleanup, material staging, and limited work hours. The schedule can also stretch if plumbing, waterproofing, or tile work uncovers hidden damage. A realistic timeline depends on demolition, inspections, custom materials, and drying time.
